# ClientX

> ClientX is a library for typed, declarative HTTP API clients on Python 3.12+, built on httpx2 and Pydantic v2. You declare endpoints as decorated methods with empty bodies; ClientX builds each request from the method's signature and annotations, and decodes the response into the method's return annotation.

Install with `pip install clientx`. ClientX depends on `httpx2`, which is a different package from `httpx`: import `httpx2`, not `httpx`.

A complete client:

```python
from typing import Annotated

from clientx import ClientX, Header, Query, Resource, Response, method
from pydantic import BaseModel


class User(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str


class NewUser(BaseModel):
    name: str


class Users(Resource, prefix="/users"):
    @method.get("/{user_id}")
    def retrieve(self, user_id: int) -> User:
        """Fetch one user by ID."""
        ...

    @method.get()
    def search(self, name: Annotated[str, Query(alias="q")], limit: int | None = None) -> list[User]:
        """Search users by name."""
        ...

    @method.post()
    def create(self, user: NewUser, request_id: Annotated[str | None, Header()] = None) -> User:
        """Create a user."""
        ...

    @method.patch("/{user_id}")
    def rename(self, user_id: int, changes: dict[str, str]) -> User:
        """Change some of a user's fields."""
        ...

    @method.delete("/{user_id}")
    def remove(self, user_id: int) -> None:
        """Delete a user."""
        ...


class ExampleAPI(ClientX, user_agent="example-app/1.0"):
    users = Users()

    @method.get("/health")
    def health(self) -> Response:
        """Check the service."""
        ...


# A 4xx or 5xx response raises httpx2.HTTPStatusError from any endpoint (raise_for_status=False turns it off).
with ExampleAPI("https://api.example.com", auth=("user", "secret"), timeout=10.0) as api:
    user = api.users.retrieve(42)  # GET /users/42 -> User
    matches = api.users.search("Ada")  # GET /users?q=Ada -> list[User] (limit is None, so it's left out)
    api.users.create(NewUser(name="Ada"), request_id="r-1")  # POST /users, JSON {"name":"Ada"}, header request-id
    api.users.rename(42, {"name": "Ada L."})  # PATCH /users/42 with JSON {"name":"Ada L."}
```

Rules for writing endpoints:

- Endpoint bodies never run. Write `...`, after the docstring if there is one: pyright rejects a body that's only a docstring when the return type isn't `None`. mypy reports `empty-body` for `...` bodies with a non-`None` return type, so turn that code off for client modules (`# mypy: disable-error-code="empty-body"`).
- Decorate endpoints with `@method.get(...)`, after `from clientx import method`; the module `clientx.method` has `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head` and `options`. Each takes `path` (default `""`: the base URL, or a resource's prefix itself, so `@method.get()` in a `prefix="/users"` resource is `GET /users`) and the keyword options `decoder`, `stream`, `deprecated` (a message string; each call emits a `DeprecationWarning`), `tags` (labels, each kept once; nothing in ClientX uses them yet), `timeout` (seconds or `httpx2.Timeout`; `None` means no timeout; left out, the client's is used) and `raise_for_status` (left out, the client's setting is used, which is `True` by default).
- The first parameter receives the client or resource (`self`) and must be positional. `*args` and `**kwargs` can't be endpoint parameters. Every endpoint needs a return annotation.
- The return annotation decides what the endpoint returns: `-> None` nothing, `-> Response` the response with its body read (`clientx.Response` is `httpx2.Response`; `clientx` also re-exports `Auth`, `Request` and `Timeout`), `-> str` the text, `-> bytes` the content, `-> Iterator[str]` the body streamed as lines, `-> Iterator[bytes]` streamed as chunks (`AsyncIterator[...]` for `async def` endpoints), and any other type the JSON body validated against the full annotation by a Pydantic `TypeAdapter` (models, `list[User]`, dicts, dataclasses, `TypedDict`s, `Annotated` constraints). A body that doesn't match raises `pydantic.ValidationError`, a `ValueError`. A type Pydantic can't validate raises `DefinitionError` when the class is defined. There are no decoder classes.
- `decoder=` takes any function `(response: httpx2.Response) -> T` in place of the annotation's decoding. Type checkers check that `T` matches the endpoint's annotation, at the decorator. The body is read before it runs, so it's a plain function (not `async def`), even for an `async def` endpoint. A generator decoder streams: a generator on a `def` endpoint annotated `-> Iterator[...]`, an async generator on an `async def` endpoint annotated `-> AsyncIterator[...]`. A decoder on an endpoint annotated `-> None` raises `DefinitionError`.
- `stream=True`, only with `-> Response` and no `decoder=`, returns the open, unread response: the caller reads it (`iter_bytes()`, `iter_lines()`) and must close it. A streamed iterator closes its response when iteration ends, breaks or fails, or when the iterator is closed.
- Where each parameter goes, as FastAPI decides it, in reverse: (1) a parameter named like a `{placeholder}` fills it; (2) a parameter with a helper in its outermost `Annotated` goes where the helper says: `Url()` (a placeholder's value), `Query()`, `Header()`, `Json()` (the JSON body or one of its fields), `Body()` (the raw body: `str`, `bytes` or an iterable of `bytes`), `Form()` (a form field), `File()` (a file in a multipart form); (3) any other parameter goes to the JSON body if its type is a model, mapping, collection or dataclass (or a union with one), and to the query string otherwise. A parameter's name, such as `json` or `headers`, has no meaning of its own. A list without a helper goes to the JSON body, so a list query parameter is `Annotated[list[str] | None, Query()] = None`.
- The helpers wrap `pydantic.Field` and take its arguments. The name a value is sent under is `alias=`: `Annotated[int, Query(alias="userId")]`. A default goes after `=` (`page: Annotated[int, Query()] = 1`); a default inside the helper, such as `Query(1)` or `Query("userId")`, raises `DefinitionError`. A `description=` or constraint such as `ge=1` isn't checked before sending.
- Path values become text (an `Enum` its value, a `datetime` ISO 8601, a number or `bool` JSON text) and are percent-encoded as one segment, so `/`, `?`, `#` and `..` in a value can't change the path. Don't pre-encode values: `%` would be encoded again. `{name:path}` keeps slashes for a value such as a file path. `{{` and `}}` are literal braces; any other brace or converter raises `DefinitionError`. Placeholders in a resource prefix count too, and every placeholder needs a parameter, which must be a plain value with no helper other than `Url()`. A `None` or empty value, or a `{name:path}` value with a leading, trailing or doubled slash, raises `ArgumentError` (with `.parameter`) before sending.
- Query parameters, headers and form fields are sent under the alias, or else the parameter's name; a header's name has underscores turned into hyphens (`request_id` becomes `request-id`). A list repeats a query parameter or form field (`?tag=a&tag=b`); a header takes a plain value only. Values become text as path values do. `None` is left out; any other default is sent. The client's own `params=` and `headers=` are sent too.
- A request has one kind of body: JSON, raw `Body()` content (at most one), or a form (`Form()` fields, and `File()` files for a multipart form); two kinds raise `DefinitionError`. A lone JSON parameter that isn't a plain value is the whole body; otherwise each JSON parameter is a field of a JSON object, under its alias or name. Values are dumped as Pydantic dumps them in JSON mode, models by alias; a model's `None` field is sent as `null`, but a parameter that's `None` is left out. There's no `DumpConfig`, `exclude_unset` or explicit `null` yet (#135): for a partial update, send a `dict` of the fields to change.
- A model, dataclass or mapping marked `Query()`, `Header()` or `Form()` is spread into that part: each field is a separate value, under its alias or name (hyphens for headers), and must be a plain value or, except in a header, a list of them; `None` fields are left out. A helper on a model's field raises `DefinitionError`: the parameter's helper decides where all of its fields go.
- One helper per parameter, in the outermost `Annotated`, around the full type with `None` inside (`Annotated[int | None, Query()]`). A helper nested inside another type (`Annotated[int, Query()] | None`, `list[Annotated[str, Query()]]`) raises `DefinitionError`; with several helpers, the last one wins. Pydantic metadata such as `Field(ge=1)` isn't a helper and can go anywhere. Reuse annotations with `type` aliases: `type UserId = Annotated[int, Query(alias="userId")]`, or `type HeaderValue[T] = Annotated[T, Header()]`.
- The helpers are named like FastAPI's but build the outgoing request. In a FastAPI app, import ClientX's under another name (`from clientx import Query as ClientQuery`) or use `clientx.Query()`.
- Resources group endpoints: `class Users(Resource, prefix="/users")`, mounted as an instance (`users = Users()`) on a client or on another resource. Prefixes are absolute (they're not combined when nesting); put an API-wide prefix such as `/v1` in the base URL. A resource subclass inherits its parent's prefix unless it sets its own, and the prefix applies only to endpoints in its own body. A resource's `tags=` go before each endpoint's own, and a subclass's tags are added to its parent's, each tag once. Calling an endpoint on a resource that isn't mounted raises `DefinitionError`. An endpoint belongs to the class whose body it's in: a second name there (`QueryDevices = query_devices`) is fine, but putting it in another class raises `DefinitionError` (declare it again there).
- Clients and resources can have plain, undecorated methods, which call endpoints through `self`. Use them to normalize arguments (endpoint bodies never run, and ClientX sends values as given) and for pagination: a `next` URL can't be passed back as a path value, which is percent-encoded, so read its query parameters with `httpx2.URL(next).params` and call the list endpoint.
- A `ClientX` is an `httpx2.Client`, so an endpoint or mounted resource on a client can't use any name the client has: `get`, `post`, `send`, `headers`, `close`, and the rest of httpx2's raise `DefinitionError`. They're free on a resource. An endpoint's name also hides that name for the rest of the class body: with bare imports (`from clientx.method import get`), a method called `get` replaces the decorator; a method called `list` makes a later `list[Post]` fail with `TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable` (define it last, or write `builtins.list[Post]`).

Using clients:

- `ClientX(base_url, *, user_agent=None, raise_for_status=None, **options)`: `base_url` is required, and every other keyword is an `httpx2.Client` option (`auth`, `headers`, `params`, `cookies`, `timeout`, `verify`, `proxy`, `transport`, `mounts`, `event_hooks`, `follow_redirects`...). A client is an `httpx2.Client`, so its settings can be changed after it's created, and `api.get(url)` sends a one-off httpx2 request (not decoded, and it doesn't raise for a 4xx or 5xx). `user_agent=` is the only class argument (`class ExampleAPI(ClientX, user_agent="example-api/1.0")`); a subclass keeps its parent's, and any other keyword in the class statement raises `TypeError: ...__init_subclass__() takes no keyword arguments`. The `User-Agent` is the `user_agent` argument, else one in `headers=`, else the class's, else `ClientX/<version>`. A client's `repr` hides a password in the base URL. Close a client with `with` or `close()`; a long-lived client (web app, worker) is created once, reused, and closed at shutdown; a closed client can't be reused (`RuntimeError`).
- Async: subclass `AsyncClientX` (an `httpx2.AsyncClient`, with the same arguments) and write endpoints as `async def` methods with the same decorators. `await api.users.retrieve(42)` returns the decoded value, and `asyncio.gather(...)` sends requests concurrently. Group async endpoints with `AsyncResource`, which mounts only on an `AsyncClientX` or another `AsyncResource`. An endpoint of the wrong kind for its class, a resource mounted on the other kind, or a class that subclasses both kinds raises `DefinitionError` when the class is defined. Stream with `-> AsyncIterator[str]` and `async for line in await api.events()`. Close with `async with` or `await client.aclose()`. Transports and event hooks must be async. Test with anyio's pytest plugin, which comes with httpx2: `@pytest.mark.anyio async def test_...`.
- Authentication: pass credentials with `auth=` when creating the client, never as endpoint parameters. `auth=` is httpx2's authentication option; for what it accepts and how to write an `Auth` subclass, see https://pydantic.dev/docs/httpx2/advanced/authentication/. Don't add credentials in a request event hook: a request hook runs again for each redirect, putting back the `Authorization` header httpx2 drops for another host. Use a third-party library's `Auth` class, not its client class.
- Status codes: a 4xx or 5xx response raises `httpx2.HTTPStatusError` from every endpoint, with the body already read (`error.response.json()` works) and before anything is decoded. A redirect isn't an error. A streamed error response is read and closed before raising. Turn it off for a client with `ClientX(..., raise_for_status=False)`, or per endpoint with `@method.get(..., raise_for_status=False)` (the endpoint's setting wins); an error response is then decoded like any other, so annotate the endpoint `-> Response`.
- Test clients without the network: `ExampleAPI("https://api.example.com", transport=httpx2.MockTransport(handler))`, where `handler(request: httpx2.Request) -> httpx2.Response` records each request (assert on `request.method`, `request.url.path`, `request.url.params`, `request.headers`, `request.content`) and returns the response to decode, or a 4xx to test `HTTPStatusError`. For a streaming endpoint, give the response an iterator of bytes (`content=iter([b"a\n"])`).
- Errors: ClientX raises `DefinitionError` (a `TypeError`) and `ArgumentError` (a `ValueError`), both `clientx.ClientXError`. `DefinitionError` is raised when the class is defined for a mistake in an endpoint, a path, a helper or a class, and at call time for an endpoint on an unmounted resource. `ArgumentError` is raised before sending for a path value that would change the path. A response that doesn't match the annotation raises `pydantic.ValidationError`. HTTP errors come from httpx2: `HTTPStatusError`, and `RequestError` for connection errors and timeouts. Annotations are evaluated when the method is decorated, so `from __future__ import annotations` works, but the types they name must be module-level and defined before the class.
- Logging: ClientX doesn't log. httpx2 logs each request at `INFO` on the `httpx2` logger, with the full URL, query string included. For your own request logging, pass httpx2 `event_hooks`.
- Not in ClientX 0.1.0: decoder classes (`ModelDecoder`, `TypeAdapterDecoder`...), `DumpConfig`, `PathParam` (use `Url()`), `validate_arguments=` (#136), a `base_url=` class argument, `DeprecatedMessage`, a `clientx` logger, and `clientx.tools` / `clientx.mcp` (#138).

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/README.md): overview, install, and a quickstart
- [Defining endpoints](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/endpoints.md): verb decorators and their options, the rules for an endpoint method, mypy, deprecation, endpoint names, one-off requests
- [Building requests](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/requests.md): where each parameter goes, the helpers, path parameters, query parameters and headers, bodies, spreading a model
- [Responses](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/responses.md): return annotations, typed results, streaming, the open response, your own decoder, errors for 4xx and 5xx
- [Resources](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/resources.md): path prefixes, nesting, plain methods for pagination and normalizing arguments
- [Client configuration](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/configuration.md): creating and closing a client, the user_agent class argument, authentication (auth=, with links to httpx2's auth docs), logging and event hooks
- [Async clients](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/async.md): AsyncClientX and AsyncResource for async def endpoints, concurrent requests, async streaming, testing
- [Testing](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/testing.md): MockTransport, checking requests, streaming responses
- [Errors](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/docs/errors.md): every error ClientX raises, and when
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/slatecipher/ClientX/blob/mainline/CHANGELOG.md): changes in each release; the API may change between minor versions before 1.0
